column1: # Whizbang performance baseline. One measure per line, tab separated:
# The value is what the measure read when the line was last written, and is reported as drift on
# every run. The CEILING is the gate, and is deliberately optional: a measure with no ceiling is
# recorded and never fails a run. Declare one only where the number is a property of the design
# rather than of the machine, and say why in the note -- a ceiling that encodes a machine's speed
# will either flap or hide a real regression, which is the failure mode this file exists to avoid.
# Values are WORK DONE (tuples, scans, blocks, rows), never wall clock. Time moves with the runner,
# its neighbors and its cache; a plan's page and tuple counts do not.
# Eight streams carrying 2,500 settled rows each in all three queue tables, none of them in the
# stream ledger, so every ring takes the deterministic-target branch. A ring names streams and must
# cost what it names, never what those streams have accumulated.
# Before the deterministic branch stopped recovering a stream's partition number by reading the
# queue table, the same scenario read 20,000 tuples and took one sequential scan PER RING on each
# of the three branches. That is the measurement this suite exists to have caught.
# The ceiling is on tuples read, and it is a property of the design: the partition number is a
# total function of the stream id, so a ring has no reason to read a queue row at all. A hundred
# leaves room for a planner that reads a page to answer something else while still being two orders
# of magnitude below a scan of a 20,000-row table. Scan counts are recorded without a ceiling,
# because they are the same finding counted a second way and one gate per family is enough.
